st.3: The gap between Neolithic Mehrgarh and the urban phase has not yet been fully bridged.

x: All three statements are correct: Kalibangan and Kot Diji anticipate Mature Harappan forms, which points to gradual, local urbanisation, though a gap between Neolithic Mehrgarh and the urban phase still remains.

st.1: Dholavira (2019) is the only inscribed Harappan World Heritage Site in India.
st.3: Harappa was inscribed in 1980.

x: None of the statements is correct: Dholavira was inscribed in 2021, not 2019; Rakhigarhi is not on the World Heritage List; it was Mohenjodaro (in Pakistan), not Harappa, that was inscribed in 1980.

st.1: The DNA came from a man who lived about 4,600 years ago.

x: Neither statement is correct: the DNA came from a woman, not a man, who lived about 4,600 years ago; her DNA showed no Steppe Pastoralist component.

st.4: Only the Bharata king Divodasa is called ardhadeva (demi-god).
st.2: His chief queen was called Parivrikti.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the chief queen was the Mahisi (Parivrikti was the discarded wife); the Rajan was a ruler of people, not of a fixed territory; it is the Puru king Trasadasyu, not Divodasa, who is called ardhadeva.

st.1: Polygamy was the usual form of marriage.
st.2: Niyoga was the choice of a husband by a girl in an open assembly.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: monogamy, not polygamy, was the usual form of marriage; niyoga was the union of a childless widow with her husband's brother (choosing a husband was swayamvara); the position of women declined, not improved, in the Later Vedic period.

st.3: Barley was called yava.

x: All three statements are correct: rice (vrihi) had ritual use, rice remains of the 8th century BCE come from Hastinapur and Atranjikhera, and yava meant barley (wheat was godhuma).

st.1: The Chhandogya Upanishad places the Chandala among the twice-born (dvija).

x: Neither statement is correct: the Chhandogya Upanishad refers to the Chandala as a person of despised birth, outside the twice-born; untouchability did not take formal shape in the Rigvedic period but only later.

st.4: His last words, 'appamadena sampadetha', were addressed to Sariputta at Kushinagar.
st.1: By tradition he was born in 563 BC and died in 483 BCE at Vaishali at the age of 80.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: he died at Kushinagar, not Vaishali; he attained enlightenment at 35, not 29; Sariputta had died before him, and his last words were addressed to the assembled monks.

st.4: The reclining Buddha in the Mahaparinirvana Temple at Kushinagar is of black basalt.
st.3: Sarnath, the place of the first sermon, was also known as Uruvela.
st.1: Lumbini, the Buddha's birthplace, is today called Piprahwa in Uttar Pradesh.

x: None of the statements is correct: Lumbini is today Rumindei (Rummindei) in Nepal; Uruvela (Bodh Gaya) on the Niranjana is the place of enlightenment, while the Rijupalika is linked with Mahavira; Sarnath was known as Rishipatana, not Uruvela; the Kushinagar reclining Buddha is of Chunar sandstone, not basalt.

st.3: He did not make belief in God a requirement for Sangha membership.

x: All three statements are correct: the Buddha neither affirmed nor denied God, likened his teaching to a raft (upaya), and did not require belief in God for entry into the Sangha.

st.3: Salihundam in Andhra was a Digambara Jaina centre.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Salihundam was a Buddhist (Vajrayana) centre, not a Jaina one; the sixth paramita is prajna (wisdom), not moksha.

st.3: Ashoka sent Mahinda and Sanghamitta to Sri Lanka.

x: All three statements are correct: the Mahavamsa credits Mahadeva Bhikshu of Andhra, Buddhism spread along the Kushan-era Silk Route, and Ashoka sent Mahinda and Sanghamitta to Sri Lanka.

st.2: Megasthenes says the Mauryas had a detailed written code of law.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Megasthenes says there was no written code of law; the parivrajika was a wandering (sanchara) spy, not a stationary one.

st.3: At Kanaganahalli, near Sannati on the Krishna, a stone portrait of Ashoka with his queens bears the label 'Ranyo Asoko'.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Maski edict was found in 1915, not 1837; Kanaganahalli near Sannati is on the Bhima, not the Krishna.

st.3: Chandragupta I married Kumaradevi, a Lichchhavi princess.

x: All three statements are correct: Duttadevi was Samudragupta's queen, Anantadevi was Kumaragupta I's queen, and Kumaradevi, whom Chandragupta I married, was a Lichchhavi princess.

st.3: The Mandasor inscription of 473 CE records silk weavers who had migrated from Gujarat (Lata) to Malwa.

x: All three statements are correct: land grants weakened the army, the loss of western India cut trade income, and the Mandasor record shows silk weavers moving from Gujarat (Lata) to Malwa.

st.3: The Virupaksha temple at Aihole, built by his queen, copies the Kailasanatha of Kanchi.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: he left a Kannada, not Tamil, inscription on the Kailasanatha pillar at Kanchi; the Virupaksha temple built by his queen Lokamahadevi is at Pattadakal, not Aihole.

st.3: He abolished mutilation (cutting of hands and feet) as a punishment.

x: All three statements are correct: his kotwals listed the unemployed for jobs, he laid out about 1,200 gardens near Delhi, and he abolished mutilation as a punishment.

st.1: His Majma-ul-Bahrain is a Persian translation of the Upanishads.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: his Persian translation of the Upanishads is the Sirr-i-Akbar (the Majma-ul-Bahrain compares Sufism and Vedanta); he was the eldest, not the second, son of Shah Jahan.

st.2: The qabuliyat was the deed of agreement and the patta the title deed.

x: All three statements are correct: land was measured with the Ilahi Gaz, the patta was the title deed and the qabuliyat the deed of agreement, and Khwaja Shah Mansoor and Muzaffar Khan Turbati helped Todar Mal.

st.4: The Tobacco Board is located at Rajahmundry.
st.2: Diamonds were mined at Motupalli.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Motupalli was a port known for the copper trade (diamonds came from the Kollur mines); Nirmal was famous for swords and Warangal for carpets, not the reverse; the Tobacco Board is at Guntur (Rajahmundry has the Central Tobacco Research Institute).

st.3: Banjar was land left fallow for five years or more.

x: All three statements are correct: polaj was cultivated every year, chachar was fallow for three to four years, and banjar was fallow for five years or more.

st.3: In prison he composed the Sumati Satakam, poems to Rama.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: he was jailed by Abul Hasan Tana Shah, not Abdullah Qutb Shah; in prison he composed the Dasarathi Satakam (the Sumati Satakam is ascribed to Baddena).

st.3: Iltutmish was also a contemporary of the Chishti saint Bahauddin Zakariya.
st.1: Moinuddin Chishti came to India with the army of Mahmud of Ghazni.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Moinuddin Chishti came with the army of Muhammad Ghori in 1192, not Mahmud of Ghazni; Bahauddin Zakariya was a Suhrawardi, not a Chishti, saint; Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi was a contemporary of Muhammad bin Tughlaq and Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

st.1: The Wavell Plan and the Simla Conference failed in 1946.
st.2: Mountbatten replaced Wavell after Churchill's statement of 20 February 1947.
st.4: Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first and last Indian Governor-General.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Simla Conference failed in 1945; the statement of 20 February 1947 was Attlee's, not Churchill's; Minto II was followed by Hardinge II, not Chelmsford; C. Rajagopalachari, not Rajendra Prasad, was the first and last Indian Governor-General.

st.1: It is an attached office of the Ministry of Tourism.
st.2: Its motto is 'Yogakshemam Vahamyaham'.

x: None of the statements is correct: the ASI is an attached office of the Ministry of Culture, not Tourism; its motto is 'Pratnakirti Apavarini'; the AMASR Act protects monuments more than 100 years old, not 50.

st.2: The High Courts at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras had been set up in 1862, before his tenure.

x: All three statements are correct: Lawrence followed 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan, the presidency High Courts dated from 1862, before him, and the Bhutan (Duar) War was fought in his time.

st.2: The Hunter Commission (1882) appointed by him examined education.

x: All three statements are correct: Ripon was sent by Gladstone's Liberal government, the Hunter Commission of 1882 examined education, and in 1882 revenue heads were divided into imperial, provincial and divided heads.

st.4: The zamindar paid 1/11 of the rental and kept 10/11.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the settlement covered about 19 per cent, not 30 per cent, of British India; the zamindar paid 10/11 of the rental and kept only 1/11.

st.1: In the Great Bengal Famine of 1770 about one-third of the people died, so revenue collection was suspended.
st.2: The Chalisa famine is named after its forty-day duration.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: in 1770 revenue was still collected despite the deaths; the Chalisa famine is named after Vikram Samvat 1840, not a forty-day span; the Great Famine of 1876-78 occurred under Lytton, not Ripon.

st.4: The maximum age for the civil service examination was 19 in 1859.
st.1: The Indian National Congress demanded simultaneous civil service examinations from its first session at Calcutta in 1885.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the first session of 1885 was at Bombay, not Calcutta; Indians outnumbered Europeans in the ICS only on 1 January 1941; the maximum age was 23 in 1859 (it was cut to 19 in 1878).

st.1: In the 1923 elections, boycotted by the Congress, it won 63 of the 98 seats.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: the 63 of 98 seats were won in the 1920 elections, not 1923; the party formed the government four times, not five.

st.3: The cradle of the Telugu language movement was North Coastal Andhra (Vizianagaram, Srikakulam, Parlakimidi).

x: All three statements are correct: Rajahmundry was the first renaissance centre (peak 1870-1935), the Kavi Club was founded at Kumudavalli in 1897, and North Coastal Andhra was the cradle of the language movement.

st.2: He rejected Gandhi's term 'Harijan' for the depressed classes.

x: All three statements are correct: Ambedkar made the 'fleeting phantoms' remark in 1931, rejected the term 'Harijan', and held that only the destruction of caste could emancipate the outcaste.

st.3: The speeches were delivered on a route from Colombo through South India to Almora.

x: All three statements are correct: the book collects Vivekananda's speeches made after his return in 1897 on his way from Colombo through South India to Almora.

st.1: He passed the ICS in 1863 and was dismissed in 1874.
st.2: His Indian National Conference merged with the INC in 1892.
st.4: He started the Amrita Bazar Patrika in 1879.

x: None of the statements is correct: he passed the ICS in 1869 (1863 was Satyendranath Tagore); the Indian National Conference merged with the INC in 1886; he presided at Poona (1895) and Ahmedabad (1902), not Surat (1907, Rash Behari Ghosh); he started The Bengalee in 1879 (the Amrita Bazar Patrika was the Ghosh brothers').

st.1: It was also called the Howrah-Sibpur conspiracy.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: it was called the Manicktolla or Muraripukur conspiracy (the Howrah case was a separate trial of 1910); Aurobindo Ghosh was acquitted, not convicted.

st.2: Azad shot himself in a police encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad, on 23 March 1931.
st.4: Sukhdev taught at the Kashi Vidyapith, Banaras.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Azad died on 27 February 1931 (23 March 1931 was the day Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged); Rajguru was born at Khed near Pune (Banga was Bhagat Singh's birthplace); Sukhdev taught at the National College, Lahore.

st.4: The mill owners were led by Anasuya Sarabhai.
st.2: A tribunal finally awarded a 20 per cent rise.
st.1: The workers demanded a 50 per cent wage rise while the owners offered 35 per cent.

x: None of the statements is correct: the owners offered 20 per cent, not 35; the tribunal awarded 35 per cent, not 20; the strike lasted about three weeks, not 35 days; the owners were led by Ambalal Sarabhai, while his sister Anasuya Sarabhai stood with the workers.

st.2: The No-changers favoured entering the councils and gave up their boycott.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the No-changers opposed council entry, favouring constructive work and continued boycott.

st.1: Gandhi was the sole representative of the Congress, and he attended all three Round Table Conferences.
st.3: The conference reached agreement on separate electorates for the minorities.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Second RTC was the only one Gandhi attended; Sarojini Naidu and Madan Mohan Malaviya, not Rajendra Prasad, went with him; the conference deadlocked over separate electorates rather than agreeing on them.

st.2: It accepted dominion status as the goal for India.

x: All three statements are correct: Linlithgow made the offer on 8 August 1940, it named dominion status (not complete independence) as the goal, and it gave the minorities a veto over any constitution.

st.1: Its plan was announced on 16 May 1946.

x: All three statements are correct: Attlee announced the mission on 19 February 1946, it reached Delhi on 24 March 1946, and its plan was announced on 16 May 1946.

st.1: Punjab, NWFP, Bengal
st.3: Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP, Sindh

x: In the Cabinet Mission Plan, Section A was Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, CP and Orissa; Section B was Punjab, NWFP and Sindh; Section C was Bengal and Assam; the Union of India held Defence, Foreign Affairs and Communications. Bengal belonged to Section C and Sindh to Section B, so the first and third entries of List-II as given do not match any unit.

st.1: Power was to be transferred on the basis of the Government of India Act, 1919.
st.3: The date of transfer was postponed from 15 August 1947 to June 1948.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: power was to be transferred on the basis of dominion status, with the Government of India Act, 1935 as the interim constitution; the date was advanced from June 1948 to 15 August 1947; Boundary Commissions were set up for both Punjab and Bengal.

st.4: Ramnagar had a parallel assembly of self-rule open only to the upper castes.
st.2: At midnight of 25 April 1921, all 15,326 residents left their homes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: 13,572 of the 15,326 residents, not all of them, left their homes; the stay at Ramnagar lasted about eleven months, not three; Ramnagar's parallel assembly was open to all castes.

st.1: Gam Mallu Dora was killed in an encounter in September 1923.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct: Gam Mallu Dora was captured, not killed, in September 1923, and it was he, not Gam Gantam Dora, who became a Member of Parliament in 1952.

st.1: Harijan Bandhu was in Hindi and Harijan Sevak in Gujarati.
st.3: The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi in English run to 50 volumes, published by the Publications Division.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Harijan Bandhu was in Gujarati and Harijan Sevak in Hindi; the autobiography was written in Gujarati and translated into English by Mahadev Desai; the Collected Works run to 100 volumes, not 50.

st.4: Ahimsa, for him, is a quality of the weak, not of the strong.
st.3: Between cowardice and violence, he said he would choose cowardice.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: 'God is Truth' was the earlier formulation and 'Truth is God' the later one; between cowardice and violence he would choose violence; ahimsa for him was a quality of the strong, not the weak.

st.4: He ended the fast on Jawaharlal Nehru's appeal.
st.1: Swami Sitaram was Ayyadevara Kaleswara Rao.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Swami Sitaram was Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri; his demand was a separate Andhra State, not the merger of Telangana; he ended the fast on Vinoba Bhave's appeal, not Nehru's.

st.3: It was signed by eight leaders, five from Andhra and three from Telangana.
st.1: It was signed at Raj Bhavan, Hyderabad.

x: None of the statements is correct: it was signed at Hyderabad House, New Delhi; it was not modelled on the Lucknow Pact; the eight signatories were four each from Andhra and Telangana.

st.3: Under Section 82 employees of State PSUs continue in their posts for three years.
st.2: Under Section 50 arrears of taxes other than property tax are divided in the ratio of population.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: under Section 50 such arrears go by the place of assessment, not by population; under Section 82 PSU employees continue for one year, not three; an order under Section 108 can be made only within two years of the appointed day.

st.2: The Nigama Sabha is named in the Nanaghat inscription.
st.1: The Nigama Sabha ran villages, and its members were Gahapatis.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Nigama Sabha ran towns, not villages; it is named in the Bhattiprolu inscription; the Gulmika headed a gulma (military outpost), while the village headman was the Gramika.

st.2: The route from Ujjain to Bharuch ran via Dhanyakataka and Vengi.
st.1: The Ikshvakus were famed as road builders ('Mahapatha nirmatalu').

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Satavahanas, not the Ikshvakus, were the famed road builders; the Ujjain-Bharuch route ran via Paithan and Tagara; the Constantine gold coin of Kudali Sangameswaram belongs to a later period.

st.1: Guilds took deposits and lent at 12% a month.
st.3: A second deposit of 1,000 karshapanas was made at 1.5% a month.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the rate was 12% a year (1% a month), not a month; the second deposit was at three-fourths of 1% a month; Ushavadatta was Nahapana's son-in-law, not his son.

st.2: They were brought to light by Mallampalli Somasekhara Sarma.
st.4: The lion is the only symbol found on them.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the coins were found by Rayaprolu Subrahmanyam; sixteen types, not twelve, are known; besides the lion they bear Nandi, ship and conch symbols.

st.2: Ibn Khurdadhbih called the Gurjara king the greatest king of India, the 'king of kings'.

x: Neither statement is correct: Sulaiman visited in 851, not 916, in Amoghavarsha I's reign; Ibn Khurdadhbih gave that title to the Balhara (the Rashtrakuta king), not the Gurjara king.

st.3: Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen sacred bathing places of the kingdom.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Sthanadhipati managed temples and their endowments, not tolls; the Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen administrative offices.

st.2: Prola II developed Hanamkonda and built the Thousand Pillar temple there.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Prola II built the Swayambhu temple in Orugallu, while the Thousand Pillar temple was Rudradeva's (1163); the name Sultanpur was given after 1323, after the Tughlaq conquest.

st.1: Mula Balam was the army supplied by the Nayankara chiefs.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Mula Balam was the king's own standing army; Gangaya Sahini was the Ashwa Sahini (cavalry), while Jayapa Senani was the Gaja Sahini.

st.3: According to legend, Lord Venkateswara of Tirumala told the king in a dream to write it during the Kalinga campaign.
st.4: Its title, Amuktamalyada, refers to its hero Vishnuchitta.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the work was dedicated to Lord Venkateswara, not Virupaksha; the dream legend names Andhra Mahavishnu of Srikakulam, not Venkateswara; the title refers to the heroine Andal, the one who offered the garland she had worn, and it is the first Telugu work named after its heroine.

st.1: It was granted by Tirumala Nayaka of Madurai.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Madras was granted to Francis Day by Damarla Venkatadri Nayaka of Srikalahasti, not Tirumala Nayaka; it was in the time of Venkatapati III, not Venkatapati Raya II (d. 1614).

st.1: Its headquarters was Rachakonda, near Bhadrachalam.
st.3: The Kaluvacheru grant (1423) of the Musunuri queen Anitalli names the 75 Nayakas who backed Prolaya Nayaka.

x: None of the statements is correct: the headquarters was Rekapalli, not Rachakonda; the confederacy was led by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka, not Koppula Prolaya Nayaka; Anitalli, who issued the Kaluvacheru grant, was a Reddi queen, not a Musunuri one.

st.1: Kapaya Nayaka's Vilasa grant gave the village Vilasa to the Brahmin Vennama.
st.3: Sangeeta Sudhakaram is a commentary on Bharata's Natyashastra.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Vilasa grant was issued by Prolaya Nayaka, not Kapaya Nayaka; Sangeeta Sudhakaram was written by Singabhupala II, not Singabhupala I; it is a commentary on Sarngadeva's Sangita Ratnakara, not the Natyashastra.

st.4: It upheld the Vedas but rejected caste, child marriage and sacrifice.
st.1: It was founded by Basaveshwara, a minister of the Hoysala Vishnuvardhana.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Basaveshwara was a minister of the Kalachuri Bijjala, not the Hoysalas; Satanis were Vaishnava followers, not Veerashaivas; Veerashaivism rejected the Vedas as well as caste, child marriage and sacrifice.

st.1: Textiles ranked second only to saltpetre in the Qutb Shahi economy.
st.2: 'Pintado' meant a woven silk textile.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: textiles ranked second only to diamonds; 'pintado' meant a printed textile; elephants were imported from Ceylon, not Persia (Persia sent horses).

st.1: Collectors lost their judicial powers under the Madras Regulations of 1816.

x: All three statements are correct: Munro's Judicial Commission (1814, report April 1816) led to the 1816 Regulations, which made Munsiff and Panchayat courts the courts of first instance and took judicial powers away from the Collectors.

st.2: After the Second Carnatic War the British installed Muhammad Ali as Nawab of the Carnatic.

x: All three statements are correct: Nellore and Chittoor came by the treaty with Azim-ud-Daula, the British installed Muhammad Ali (Chanda Sahib was the French candidate), and before 1794 the Circars were run by Chiefs and Councils.

st.1: Radhakrishna Dandasena's rising at Parlakimidi was a Koya rising, put down by Captain Wilson.
st.2: Korukonda Subba Reddy, a village official of Karaturu, rose on rumours of Tantia Tope's advancing army.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Dandasena's rising was a Savara, not a Koya, rising; Subba Reddy rose on rumours of Nana Saheb's, not Tantia Tope's, army; the Faujdari Adalat was a court, not the centre of any movement.

st.1: He was knighted in 1878.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Cotton was knighted in 1861, not 1878; on his suggestion Rajahmundry district became Godavari and Machilipatnam district became Krishna, not the reverse.

st.4: Idukallu Sadasivan organised the 1937 political summer school at Kothapatnam.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Yuva Mahasabhas were held at Vizag in 1935 and Kakinada in 1936, not the reverse; Idukallu Sadasivan organised the 1938 school at Hindupur, while Kothapatnam (1937) was the first summer school.

st.2: He was born at Rayavaram and was in the court of the Raja of Pithapuram.
st.3: He wrote the English poem Mutyala Saralu.
st.1: His play Kanyasulkam, on bride-price, was written in 1892 and first staged at Rajahmundry.

x: None of the statements is correct: Kanyasulkam was first staged at Vizianagaram; he was in the court of Ananda Gajapati of Vizianagaram; his English poem was Sarangadhara (Mutyala Saralu is Telugu verse); he championed the spoken (vyavaharika) idiom, not only the granthika.

st.1: In January 2022 the AP government banned the staging of Chintamani.

x: All three statements are correct: the 2022 ban was on Chintamani (over Subbi Setty), Viplava Parivartanamu was banned during the NCM, and Gollapudi Sitarama Sastri backed the 1920 election boycott.

st.1: Gurajada Apparao wrote the first book on the theory of folk knowledge in Telugu.
st.2: World Folk Day is observed on 22 April.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the first book on folk theory was by Biruduraju Ramaraju; World Folk Day is 22 August; jola patalu are lullabies, not harvest songs.

st.2: Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar moved on to Virasam in 1965.
st.1: Cherabandaraju stayed away from Virasam when it was formed in 1970.

x: Neither statement is correct: Cherabandaraju, Jwalamukhi and Nikhileswar all moved on to Virasam when it was formed in 1970 (1965 was the year the Digambara group arose).

st.2: They blocked the Silk Road trade between Han China and Rome.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the Kushanas were Silk Road middlemen between Han China, Rome and India, not a barrier to that trade; their empire extended well beyond the Indus into the Gangetic plain.

st.2: In Andhra history he is linked with Sriparvata and the Vakataka court.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: Nagarjuna is linked with Sriparvata and the Satavahana court, not the Vakatakas; it was I-tsing, not Fa-hien, who saw students memorising his Suhrllekha.

st.2: They were patrons of Vaishnavism and Saivism.
st.1: They ruled the Tamil country c. 8th-10th century CE.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the Kalabhras ruled c. 3rd-6th century CE; they patronised Jainism and Buddhism, not Vaishnavism and Saivism; their rule was ended by the Pandya Kadungon and the Pallava Simhavishnu.

st.1: Ghori's first defeat came in 1191 at Kasahrada near Mount Abu during his Gujarat campaign.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the defeat at Kasahrada came in 1178 (1191 was his defeat at Tarain); Chandawar is near Firozabad in Uttar Pradesh, not Karnal.

st.1: Georg Simmel studied suicide and anomie.
st.3: Manuel Castells gave the concept of the risk society.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Simmel studied social interaction and city life (suicide and anomie were Durkheim's themes); Castells gave the network society (the risk society is Ulrich Beck's); Malinowski was a functionalist, not of the conflict school.

st.1: Rahmat Ali coined the name 'Pakistan'
st.4: The Communal Award extended separate electorates to the Depressed Classes

x: The years match as follows: 1887 - Dufferin used Syed Ahmad Khan to keep Muslims away from the Congress; 1909 - first legal separate electorate for Muslims; 1929 - Jinnah's Fourteen Points; 1930 - Iqbal proposed a consolidated Muslim state. st.4: Jyoti Basu founded the Trinamool Congress in West Bengal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the steps against regionalism list the Fifth, Sixth and Eighth Schedules, not the Eleventh; Jyoti Basu was a CPI(M) leader of West Bengal, while the Trinamool Congress was founded by Mamata Banerjee.

st.1: Leave from the third child onwards is 26 weeks.

x: Neither statement is correct: from the third child onwards leave is 12 weeks (26 weeks is for the first two); work from home after the leave is by mutual agreement, not in every case.

st.2: A heinous offence is one with a minimum punishment of ten years or more.
st.3: After the assessment, the Juvenile Justice Board may transfer the case to the Children's Court, which is a Judicial Magistrate's court.

x: None of the statements is correct: the preliminary assessment is not a finding of guilt; a heinous offence carries a minimum of seven, not ten, years; the Children's Court is a Sessions Court.

st.3: Andhra Pradesh (6.06%) was ranked 9th.

x: All three statements are correct: India's headcount was 14.96%, Bihar was highest at 33.76%, and Andhra Pradesh, at 6.06%, was ranked 9th.

st.2: Mahila Kisan Sashaktikaran Pariyojana is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development under DAY-NRLM.

x: All three statements are correct: DAY-NRLM began in 2011 as Aajeevika, MKSP is run by the Ministry of Rural Development under DAY-NRLM (not by MWCD), and the Mahila Samman Savings Certificate runs 2 years at 7.5%.

st.1: Article 45, after the 86th Amendment (2002), provides for ECCE for all children until they complete fourteen years.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Article 45 covers ECCE until the age of six, not fourteen (6-14 is Article 21A); the NEP 2020 foundational stage covers ages 3-8, not 3-10.

st.2: The Atal Pension Yojana is administered by the EPFO.
st.1: The Atal Pension Yojana replaced the PM Shram Yogi Maandhan scheme of 2019.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: APY (2015) replaced the Swavalamban scheme of 2010; it is run by PFRDA, not EPFO; its guaranteed pension is Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month, not up to Rs 10,000.

st.2: No strike can be held within 30 days of giving notice.
st.3: The threshold for contract labour provisions was raised from 20 to 30 workers.
st.1: The threshold for prior permission for layoff, retrenchment and closure was raised from 100 to 200 workers.

x: None of the statements is correct: the layoff threshold went from 100 to 300; no strike may be held within 14 days of notice; the contract labour threshold went from 20 to 50; fixed-term workers get gratuity after one year, not five.

st.3: MGNREGA is linked to SDG 1 and SDG 8.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's SSAAT pioneered MGNREGA social audits, Geo-MGNREGA geotags assets with Bhuvan, and the scheme is linked to SDG 1 and SDG 8.

st.1: e-Seva (2010) set up India's first integrated citizen service centres.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: e-Seva dates from 2001, not 2010; Village and Ward Secretariats came in 2019, not 2014.

st.3: In Bal Patil v. Union of India (2005) the Court directed the Centre to notify Jains as a minority.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: P.A. Inamdar was decided by a 7-judge Bench, not 9; in Bal Patil the Court declined to direct the Centre and left it to the States.

st.2: The National Integration Council was set up in 1961 under Lal Bahadur Shastri.
st.4: The Kundu Committee was headed by Justice Rajinder Sachar.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the National Integration Council was set up under Nehru; the National Foundation for Communal Harmony dates from 1992, not 1996; the Kundu Committee was headed by Prof. Amitabh Kundu, not Justice Sachar.

st.2: Atal Bihari Vajpayee gave the first Hindi speech at the UNGA in 1977, as Prime Minister.
st.4: That resolution had 193 co-sponsors.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: Harish has held the post since September 2024, not 2022; Vajpayee spoke as External Affairs Minister, not Prime Minister; resolution 69/131 had 177 co-sponsors, not 193.

st.4: The Emissions Gap Report 2025, published by the WMO, says current policies put the world on course for about 2.8°C.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: SOFI is published jointly by FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO, not UNEP alone; the Emissions Gap Report is published by UNEP, not the WMO.

st.1: India has ratified C87 and C98 on freedom of association and collective bargaining.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: India has not ratified C87 and C98; it ratified C138 and C182 in 2017, not 2015.

st.3: It is open to all UN members.

x: All three statements are correct: the NDB's founders hold equal votes with no veto, it is headquartered at Shanghai, and membership is open to all UN members.

st.4: It launched the IPMDA in 2024.
st.2: It was revived in 2019.
st.1: It originated as the Tsunami Core Group after the 2011 Japan tsunami.

x: None of the statements is correct: the Quad grew out of the Tsunami Core Group after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami; it was revived in 2017; its first leaders' summit (March 2021) was virtual, the first in-person one being at Washington in September 2021; the IPMDA was launched in 2022.

st.2: Under the B-R-I-C-S rotation, China will chair BRICS in 2027.

x: All three statements are correct: Kazan hosted the 16th summit in 2024 under Russia, China chairs in 2027, and India's 2026 theme was 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.

st.3: The SPG was formed in 1985, and the Special Protection Group Act was enacted in 1988.

x: All three statements are correct: the NIA Act came in 2008 after 26/11, the NSG (1984) is called the 'Black Cats', and the SPG was formed in 1985 with its Act following in 1988.

st.4: The Act of 1786 let the Governor-General override his Council and act as Commander-in-Chief, first used by Lord Wellesley.
st.1: Pitt's India Act, 1784 set up a nine-member Board of Control for political affairs.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Board of Control had six members, not nine; Pitt's India Act reduced the council to three members; the 1786 powers were first used by Lord Cornwallis, not Wellesley.

st.3: The President as a nominal head follows the American model of the presidency.
st.2: Parliamentary privileges were borrowed from the USA.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: parliamentary privileges and the nominal head modelled on the Crown both come from Britain, not the USA; single citizenship too is from Britain, not the USA.

st.2: It does not need the consent of the State Legislature.

x: All three statements are correct: President's Rule may be imposed on the Governor's report or otherwise, needs no consent of the State Legislature, and each parliamentary approval keeps it in force for six months.

st.1: The National Commission for Minorities is a constitutional body under Article 350B.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the NCM is a statutory body under the NCM Act, 1992 (Article 350B is the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities); the six notified communities are religious minorities, not linguistic ones.

st.2: It was passed under the Congress government of Indira Gandhi.
st.3: The omission of Article 31 took effect from 26 January 1979.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the 44th Amendment was passed under the Janata government of Morarji Desai; the omission of Article 31 took effect from 20 June 1979; after it there are six Fundamental Rights, not seven.

st.3: It does not apply to minority educational institutions referred to in Article 30(1).

x: All three statements are correct: Article 15(5) was inserted by the 93rd Amendment (2005), permits reservation in private unaided institutions, and exempts minority educational institutions.

st.1: The reservation starts from the next general election, without waiting for delimitation.

x: Neither statement is correct: the reservation begins only after delimitation based on the first Census taken after commencement; it lasts 15 years but Parliament can extend it by law.

st.2: To raise a matter in Zero Hour, a member intimates the Presiding Officer a week in advance.
st.1: An ordinary parliamentary question requires 10 clear days' notice.
st.4: In the Lok Sabha up to 10 matters a day, in order of the ballot, may be raised in Zero Hour.

x: None of the statements is correct: an ordinary question needs 15 clear days' notice; for Zero Hour the member intimates the Presiding Officer on the same day; the Chair's directions go through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, not the Cabinet Secretariat; up to 20 matters a day may be raised.

st.3: 30, drawn from both Houses
st.4: 15, chairman chosen from its Lok Sabha members

x: The Public Accounts Committee has 22 members with an Opposition chairman by convention; each Departmentally Related Standing Committee has 31; the Estimates Committee has 30, all from the Lok Sabha; the Committee on Public Undertakings has 22, its chairman chosen from its Lok Sabha members. So the third and fourth entries of List-II as given match no committee.

st.3: The 106th Amendment (2023) provides for reserving one-fourth of Assembly seats for women after delimitation.
st.1: Article 173 prescribes a minimum age of 25 years for the Legislative Council and 30 years for the Legislative Assembly.
st.2: Seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Assemblies are reserved in proportion to their population under Article 330.

x: None of the statements is correct: Article 173 sets 30 years for the Council and 25 for the Assembly; Assembly reservation is under Article 332 (330 is the Lok Sabha); the 106th Amendment reserves one-third, not one-fourth; the quorum is ten members or one-tenth, whichever is greater.

st.4: The YSRCP won 11 seats, more than one-tenth, and so is the official Opposition.
st.2: The NDA won 164 of the 175 seats, the TDP alone winning 151.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the TDP alone won 135 seats (151 was the YSRCP's 2019 tally); the Jana Sena won 21 and the BJP 8; the YSRCP's 11 seats are below one-tenth, so it has no official Opposition status.

st.2: An MP's vote value varies with the population of his constituency.
st.1: An MLA's vote value = population of the State ÷ number of elected MLAs × 1/100.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the MLA formula divides by 1,000, not 100; every MP's vote has the same value; a State's MLA vote value depends on population per seat, not simply on the number of seats.

st.2: He does not appoint the judges of the High Court; they are appointed by the President.

x: All three statements are correct: the Governor appoints the SPSC members (only the President removes them) and District Judges in consultation with the High Court, while High Court judges are appointed by the President.

st.2: H.R. Khanna
st.3: V.R. Krishna Iyer

x: H.R. Khanna and V.R. Krishna Iyer never became Chief Justice of India, so they cannot be placed in the order; of the Chief Justices named, M. Patanjali Sastri (1951-54) came before P.N. Bhagwati (1985-86).

st.1: The theory principally underlying it is the supremacy of the Constitution.

x: All three statements are correct: judicial review rests on the supremacy of the Constitution (not of Parliament), a written Constitution, federalism and Fundamental Rights, and a law can be struck down for lack of legislative competence.

st.2: It has seven members including the Chairperson.
st.3: Its Chairperson is a serving Supreme Court judge.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Commission has five members, not seven; its Chairperson is a former, not serving, Supreme Court judge or a former High Court Chief Justice; members hold office for five years or until 70, not 65.

st.1: They were constituted under Sections 408 and 410 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016.
st.4: Under the Companies Act, the limit for such an appeal is 30 days.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: NCLT and NCLAT were constituted under the Companies Act, 2013, not the IBC; the appeal limit is 30 days under IBC Section 61 and 45 days under the Companies Act.

st.2: They are not required to follow the principles of natural justice.
st.3: Their decisions are final and cannot be appealed.

x: None of the statements is correct: quasi-judicial bodies are not bound by the CPC, must follow natural justice, and their decisions are appealable.

st.1: While an Article 249 resolution is in force, the State Legislature retains its power to legislate on that matter.

x: All three statements are correct: the State keeps its power under Article 249 (the Union law prevails in conflict), the Union law ceases six months after the resolution lapses, and an Article 250 law may extend to the whole or any part of India.

st.3: The Constitution fixes the qualifications and tenure of the Special Officer.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities works under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, not Home Affairs; the Constitution does not fix the Special Officer's qualifications, tenure, salary or removal.

st.4: The Central Information Commission is a constitutional, not a statutory, body.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Article 263 is the Inter-State Council); the Central Information Commission is a statutory body under the RTI Act, not a constitutional one.

st.2: After demitting office they are ineligible for further employment under the Central or any State Government.

x: All three statements are correct: since 2019 members serve 3 years or till 70 and may be reappointed, they are barred from further government employment, Central or State, and they resign in writing to the President.

st.2: The first Lokpal Bill lapsed when the Lok Sabha was dissolved before the Rajya Sabha could pass it.

x: All three statements are correct: the first Lokpal Bill (1968) passed the Lok Sabha in 1969 and lapsed on its dissolution, not by Rajya Sabha rejection; the 30-day asset declaration was changed by the 2016 amendment.

st.1: A whistle-blower must be a public servant; NGOs and other persons are excluded.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: any public servant or other person, including an NGO, may be a whistle-blower; anonymous complaints are not accepted.

st.3: The present division of functions between the Finance Commission and the Planning Commission is unreasonable and should be changed.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Sarkaria kept residuary taxation with Parliament (only other residuary powers were to go to the Concurrent List); it found the Finance Commission - Planning Commission division reasonable and wanted it continued.

st.3: The State Finance Commission is constituted by the President every five years.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the Madhya Pradesh SEC was constituted on 1 February 1994, not 1995; the State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor, not the President.

st.3: In Scheduled Areas acquisition needs no consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: consent of 80 per cent is needed for private projects and 70 per cent for PPP projects, not the reverse; in Scheduled Areas acquisition is a last resort and needs the consent of the Gram Sabha, Panchayat or Autonomous Council.

st.4: The base year of the headline CPI used as the anchor is 2012.
st.2: Growth is the primary objective and price stability is secondary.
st.3: It is based on the Bimal Jalan Committee (2014) and was adopted in 2016.

x: None of the statements is correct: the MPC has 3 RBI and 3 external members; price stability is primary and growth secondary; the framework rests on the Urjit Patel Committee (2014); the anchor CPI now has base year 2024, not 2012.

st.1: The IEG is a society under the IT&C Department.

x: All three statements are correct: the JKCs trained college students in technical and soft skills and were run by the IEG, a society under the IT&C Department (not AP Online).

st.2: It originated in the United Kingdom in 1991 under John Major.

x: All three statements are correct: India adopted the Citizens' Charter in 1997 with DARPG coordinating, it began in the UK in 1991 under John Major (not Thatcher), and the charters are non-justiciable.

st.2: The FCRA Amendment Rules, 2026 were notified on 22 March 2026.
st.3: The Amendment Bill of 25 March 2026 proposed taking over assets of NGOs whose registration was cancelled, and was passed.
st.4: Renewal under the 2026 Rules needs ₹10 lakh spent over five years.

x: None of the statements is correct: foreign citizens other than PIOs as key functionaries make an NGO ineligible, so a PIO does not; the Rules were notified on 22 June 2026; the asset-takeover Bill was deferred, not passed; renewal needs ₹10 lakh spent over two years.

st.3: The Jal Shakti Abhiyan (2015) focused on 256 water-stressed districts.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: NWP-2012 did not replace State water institutions with a single Union authority; the Jal Shakti Abhiyan was launched in 2019, not 2015.

st.3: India was the first to invoke it, for rice, in 2020.

x: All three statements are correct: the Bali Peace Clause shields public stockholding beyond de minimis/AMS limits, covers existing programmes and traditional staples with notification, and India first invoked it for rice in 2020.

st.4: The first distribution covered 65.31 lakh beneficiaries in 18 categories.
st.1: The old-age pension was raised to ₹3,000 a month.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the old-age pension was raised to ₹4,000, not ₹3,000; fully disabled persons get ₹15,000, not ₹10,000; the first distribution covered 28 categories, not 18.

st.3: India has 5.68 lakh ODF Plus villages.

x: All three statements are correct: Saubhagya electrified all willing households, SBM-G built 12.19 crore toilets, and there are 5.68 lakh ODF Plus villages (1,288 is the number of GOBARdhan plants).

st.3: Electricity, gas and water supply is counted under Industry.

x: All three statements are correct: livestock is under agriculture and allied activities, while mining and quarrying and electricity, gas and water supply are both counted under Industry.

st.4: Capital formation depends only on savings, not on financial institutions.
st.2: Social overhead capital and human resource development lie outside the scope of development.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: social overhead capital and human resource development are part of development; workers moving out of agriculture raise overall productivity; capital formation depends on savings and on effective financial institutions.

st.2: The three pillars of India's inclusive growth model are Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism.

x: All three statements are correct: inclusive growth looks at pace and pattern, its pillars are Market Economics, Empowerment and Pragmatism (not Antyodaya), and it targets marginal farmers, landless labourers and SC/ST communities.

st.1: The 16th FC anchors the States' fiscal deficit at 4% of GSDP.
st.4: GST compensation was paid for five years, from April 2017 to March 2022.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the 16th FC anchors the States' deficit at 3% of GSDP; the extra borrowing equals NPS/UPS contributions, not EPF; GST compensation ran from July 2017 to June 2022.

st.2: India's intergovernmental transfers to local bodies are about 0.5% of GDP, against 2-5% globally.

x: All three statements are correct: transfers were about 40% of ULB revenue in the IIHS study, Indian transfers to local bodies are only about 0.5% of GDP, and weak accounting keeps local bodies out of the bond market.

st.4: It used 131 indicators aligned to MoSPI's National Indicator Framework.
st.1: It was released on 12 July 2024 and India's composite score rose to 71 from 60 in 2020-21.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the score rose to 71 from 66 in 2020-21, not 60; Bihar, not Jharkhand, was bottom-ranked; the index used 113 indicators, not 131.

st.4: It stands at 23% at present.
st.1: Its statutory range is 25% to 40% of NDTL.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: the range is 0% to 40% since the 25% floor went in 2007; the penalty is bank rate + 3% at first and bank rate + 5% if the shortfall continues; the SLR stands at 18%, not 23%.

st.3: The 2025 Act amends the Insurance Act, 1938, the LIC Act, 1956 and the IRDA Act, 1999.

x: All three statements are correct: IRDAI is headquartered at Hyderabad, the 2025 Act raised the FDI cap from 74% to 100%, and it amends all three laws.

st.2: Salaries of Supreme Court judges

x: All three are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India: pensions of High Court judges, salaries of Supreme Court judges and the Union's debt charges (salaries of High Court judges are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State).

st.3: Insurance is listed in Entry 47 of the Union List.

x: All three statements are correct: the cap went from 26% to 49% in 2015 and to 74% from 19 May 2021, and insurance is Entry 47 of the Union List, not the State List.

st.1: West Bengal was the leading rice producer in 2023-24.
st.2: Punjab was the leading rice producer in 2024-25.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Telangana led rice output in 2023-24 and Uttar Pradesh in 2024-25; Uttar Pradesh, not Punjab, is the largest wheat producer.

st.1: The Lab to Land Programme was launched in 1979.

x: All three statements are correct: Lab to Land began in 1979 (1974 was the first KVK), NATP in 1998 with World Bank aid, and NAIP ran 2006-2014.

st.2: KVIC works under the Ministry of MSME.

x: All three statements are correct: KVIC is a statutory body under the 1956 Act working under the Ministry of MSME (not Rural Development), and MSMEs contribute about 31.1% of GDP.

st.4: Its loan limit was raised from Rs 1 lakh to Rs 3 lakh in August 2026.
st.2: The effective interest rate for prompt repayers is 7%.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: prompt repayers pay an effective 4%, not 7% (the base rate); MISS is a Central Sector scheme run through RBI and NABARD; its limit went from Rs 3 lakh to Rs 5 lakh in August 2026.

st.4: They were repealed in January 2021.
st.1: The Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce Act allowed trade in a 'trade area' outside APMC yards, subject to State market fee.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: trade outside APMC yards was free of State market fee; the laws rested on Concurrent List Entry 33, not the Union List; they were repealed in November 2021 (in January 2021 the Supreme Court only stayed them).

st.2: Its three-year average turnover must exceed ₹5,000 crore.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the average turnover must exceed ₹25,000 crore; the average net profit must exceed ₹5,000 crore, not ₹15,000 crore (₹15,000 crore is the net-worth test).

st.3: It covers mining, manufacturing and construction.
st.2: It is compiled monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the basket is not 809 products; the IIP is compiled by the NSO (MoSPI), not DPIIT, which compiles the WPI; it covers mining, manufacturing and electricity, not construction.

st.2: The Foreign Investment Facilitation portal was merged with the National Single Window System in August 2022.

x: All three statements are correct: e-Biz is an NeGP Mission Mode Project, the FIF portal merged into the NSWS in August 2022, and Invest India (2009) is a not-for-profit joint venture.

st.1: Andhra Pradesh contributed about 50% of India's shrimp exports in 2024-25.

x: Neither statement is correct: AP contributed about 31%, not 50%, of shrimp exports in 2024-25; exports to China rose in 2025-26.

st.1: China was the largest destination of India's seafood exports in 2025-26.
st.3: Andhra Pradesh's fish output in 2024-25 was 42 lakh tonnes.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: China was the second-largest, not the largest, destination; AP's fish output was 55.39 lakh tonnes (42 lakh tonnes was the old 2020 target); AP's seafood exports depend heavily on the US market.

st.1: It offers 93+ clearances from 39 departments.
st.2: It gives pre-establishment and pre-operation approvals within 30 days.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: the portal covers 19 departments, not 39; approvals come within 21 days, not 30; investors need not visit regulators physically.

st.2: Its Foundational stage covers ages 3-6.
st.3: Its Middle stage covers ages 8-11.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: the Foundational stage covers ages 3-8; the Middle stage covers 11-14 (8-11 is the Preparatory stage); vocational education is integrated from Grade 6, not Grade 9.

st.2: Higher government borrowing tends to raise bond yields.

x: All three statements are correct: bond prices and yields move inversely, more government borrowing raises yields, and RBI OMO purchases lower them.

st.1: Kilimanjaro in Kenya is a dormant stratovolcano of the East African Rift.
st.3: Volcan de Fuego is linked to the subduction of the Nazca plate beneath the South American plate.

x: Only statement 4 is correct: Kilimanjaro is in Tanzania, not Kenya; Krakatoa is in Indonesia, not the Philippines; Fuego (Guatemala) is linked to the Cocos plate subducting beneath the Caribbean plate.

st.3: The Bering Sea is deeper than the Baltic Sea.

x: All three statements are correct: the Philippine Sea is the largest sea, the Sea of Azov is the shallowest, and the Bering Sea is far deeper than the Baltic.

st.2: Fronts are a feature of temperate cyclones but not of tropical cyclones.

x: All three statements are correct: air in a cyclone converges and rises, fronts occur in temperate but not tropical cyclones, and a cloudburst is a very local disturbance.

st.1: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands share maritime borders with Myanmar, Thailand and Malaysia.
st.4: Lakshadweep is a group of 36 coral islands with its capital at Agatti.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: the islands' maritime neighbours are Myanmar, Thailand and Indonesia, not Malaysia; they do not border Sri Lanka; Lakshadweep's capital is Kavaratti, not Agatti.

st.3: India's third contract (15 September 2025) is for polymetallic sulphides in the Carlsberg Ridge.

x: All three statements are correct: India became the first Pioneer Investor in 1987, its 2016 contract covers sulphides in the Central and South West Indian Ridge, and its third contract is for sulphides, not nodules, in the Carlsberg Ridge.

st.2: In winter the Indira Gandhi Canal is fed by the Pong dam on the Beas.

x: All three statements are correct: the canal takes off from Harike with a 649-km main canal, is fed in winter by the Pong dam on the Beas (not Bhakra), and the Gang Canal dates from 1927.

st.3: The heavy minerals of India's beach sands include ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and bauxite.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: India is not self-sufficient in uranium and imports it; bauxite is not a beach-sand mineral (the set is ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet, sillimanite and monazite).

st.3: Kerosene is the C10-C16 fraction of crude oil.

x: All three statements are correct: biogas is 50-75% methane from anaerobic digestion, producer gas is mainly CO and nitrogen, and kerosene is the C10-C16 fraction (C5-C10 is petrol).

st.1: The first tea plantations of India were set up in the Nilgiri hills of Tamil Nadu in the first half of the 19th century.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: India's first tea plantations were in the Brahmaputra valley of Assam, not the Nilgiris; tea was not first grown in Africa at Nairobi in 1850.

st.3: The Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 targets port capacity of 3 billion tonnes per annum.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: nationalisation of shipping is not a Sagarmala pillar; the Vision 2047 target is 10 billion tonnes per annum, not 3 billion.

st.1: Ramayapatnam port lies next to NH-65 and Thettu railway station.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct: Ramayapatnam lies next to NH-16, not NH-65; the last-mile rail links to Kopparthy, Orvakal and Krishnapatnam are still incomplete.

st.2: NEP 2020 targets a 50% Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education by 2035.

x: All three statements are correct: NEP targets 100% school GER by 2030 and 50% higher-education GER by 2035 (not 2030), and NIPUN Bharat aims at FLN by Grade 3 with its deadline moved to 2026-27.

st.3: Telangana
st.2: Ladakh

x: Ladakh and Telangana did not exist as separate units in Census 2011, so they cannot be ranked by 2011 density; of the others, Andaman and Nicobar Islands (46 per sq km) is less dense than Sikkim (86).

st.2: Agricultural labourers, not cultivators, formed the largest category of its workers.

x: All three statements are correct: AP's WPR of about 46.6% is above the national rate, agricultural labourers were its largest worker group, and its 86.12 lakh main agricultural labourers were about 45% of its main workers.

st.3: In 1961-71 AP's growth rate was lower than India's.

x: All three statements are correct: the peak of 21.13% came in 1981-91, AP grew 12.32% against India's 21.5% in 1991-2001, and in 1961-71 too AP grew more slowly than India.

st.3: Muslims had a higher sex ratio than Hindus.

x: All three statements are correct: Christians had the highest sex ratio (about 1,023), Sikhs the lowest, and Muslims (951) were above Hindus (939).

st.1: India produces about one-third of the world's castor seed.

x: Only statement 3 is correct: India produces about nine-tenths of the world's castor seed, not one-third; per OIV 2024 Italy, not France, was the largest wine producer.

st.3: Under the Ural-Kuznetsk Combine the Kuzbass sent iron ore to the Urals and received coal back.

x: Only statement 2 is correct: Kemerovo and Novokuznetsk are Kuzbass centres, not Donbas; under the Combine the Kuzbass sent coal to the Urals and received iron ore, not the reverse.

st.3: NDMA's heat-wave action-plan guidelines were last updated in 2019.

x: All three statements are correct: Heat Action Plans are made by States and cities, cool roofs are a heat-wave measure, and the NDMA guidelines were updated in 2019.

st.3: An FPGA can be re-programmed after manufacturing.

x: All three statements are correct: deep learning is a subset of machine learning, recommender systems use past behaviour, and an FPGA is field-programmable after manufacture.

st.3: 10% TDS applies on transfers.

x: Only statement 1 is correct: VDA losses cannot be set off against other income; TDS on transfers is 1%, not 10%.

st.3: It sought to spread IT activity beyond the six established hubs to Tier II and Tier III cities.

x: All three statements are correct: NPIT 2012 aimed to make India the global IT/ITES hub by 2020, noted the six hubs' 90% share and 80% export revenue, and sought to spread IT beyond those hubs.

st.3: SIGHT, with ₹17,490 crore, funds public-private partnerships for hydrogen R&D.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct: the nodal ministry is MNRE, not the Ministry of Power; SIGHT gives incentives for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production, while R&D partnerships come under SHIP.

st.1: It is slower than conventional thermal or chemical clean-up.

x: All three statements are correct: bioremediation is slower than thermal or chemical methods, handles oil spills, heavy metals, pesticides and solvents, and may use genetically engineered microbes.

st.3: Trichoderma and NPV are biopesticides, not biofertilisers.

x: All three statements are correct: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in legume nodules, cyanobacteria are paddy biofertilisers, and Trichoderma and NPV are biopesticides.

st.1: The term 'Industry 4.0' was coined in Germany at the Hannover Fair, 2016.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct: 'Industry 4.0' was coined at the Hannover Fair in 2011, not 2016 (2016 is Schwab's 'Fourth Industrial Revolution'); SAMARTH Udyog Bharat 4.0 belongs to the Ministry of Heavy Industries, not MeitY.

st.1: PaaS provides virtualised computing and storage infrastructure.
st.2: MeghRaj (GI Cloud) is a DoT initiative; NIC launched the national cloud under it in 2014.
